messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool 'prod-west-3' saturation + queue growth detected (>= 95% GPU util) — alert id 2026-03-15-INC-7721
Elijah (SRE): I'm on it. hitting high queueing and lots of 429 throttles in the gateway logs.
Maya (Oncall): Paging SRE. Noted increased 429s and long tail latencies reported by telem. Any customer-facing errors?
Lucas (Support): We already have a handful of customers reporting elevated error rates and timeouts on generation endpoints (chat & stream). CS is holding until we have a mitigation.
Elijah (SRE): Initial glance: GPU pool queued requests spiking, autoscaler hasn't been adding capacity past max_pool_size. Seeing repeated prefill patterns in logs causing per-request token counts to balloon.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Which model is hot? I can check rollout.
Elijah (SRE): Model v19.0.1 was promoted to stable ~45m ago. From traces, median input sequence length jumped from ~1024 to ~4600 for that model in the last 30m. KV-cache warmup sequence pattern visible in runtime traces: repeated prefill + long completion windows.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): That matches the deploy notes — v19 changed default context_window to 4096 for some clients and added a prefill optimization that can double prefix tokens in certain prompt patterns. Might be a runaway when combined with streaming prefill.
Maya (Oncall): TL;DR: rollout increased per-request work -> autoscaler exhausted (hit configured max) -> queue growth -> gateway 429s. Agreed?
Elijah (SRE): Yep. Also seeing autoscaler logs: "scale_request_denied: pool cap reached" and HPA metric plateau. Manual scale attempts from console are failing because pool quota for this cluster is at the committed limit.
DeployBot: Deploy v19.0.1 -> stable promoted by Zoe at 2026-03-15T02:10:23Z.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): I can rollback the rollout or flip the config to disable the prefill expansion flag. Which do we want first?
Elijah (SRE): Immediate priority is to reduce GPU pressure. Two quick options: 1) Disable the prefill expansion flag for v19 (runtime config flip, non-disruptive) OR 2) Revert rollout to v18. Both doable. Also we should throttle offending customers and enable fallback model routing to a smaller model to reduce load.
Maya (Oncall): I'll start customer throttling + global token rate cap at edge. Lucas, can you coordinate communications with affected customers?
Lucas (Support): On it. I'll post a short note and list affected org ids once we have the 5xx/429 windows.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): I can flip the prefill flag now. Patch: `PATCH /runtime/configs/v19?prefill_expansion=false` — should be hot.
Elijah (SRE): While that's rolling, can we also open a manual scale request with infra (we're at quota)? I'll escalate to infra on call. If we can temporarily increase pool cap by +4 GPUs we can buy time for a rollback if needed.
Maya (Oncall): Escalated infra: @infra-oncall can we get an emergency +4 GPU quota increase in prod-west-3? Reason: autoscaler exhausted due to increased per-request context.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Applying runtime config change now. Patch done, propagation to nodes in progress. Expect effect on new requests in ~30s-2m as connections cycle.
IncidentBot: Note: Runtime config change recorded by DeployBot. Audit id RUNTIME-6073.
Elijah (SRE): Observing queue length dropping slightly, 429 rate trending down, p95 latency still high but improving.
Lucas (Support): Draft sent to customers flagged as impacted. Mentioned rollback as a possible next step, apologized, and promised updates every 30m.
Maya (Oncall): Infra replied — we cannot expand committed GPU quota for this cluster without approval (billing/ops). They offered to spin a temporary overflow pool in another AZ but it will take ~12-18 minutes to provision. Good as contingency.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): If overflow takes that long we should schedule a rollback to v18 if the config flip doesn't fully restore capacity. Can someone prepare the revert?
Elijah (SRE): I'll prepare the revert playbook and hold off until we confirm the config flip effect. Also added a short-term inbound rate limit at the gateway: `rlimit model=v19 requests_per_minute=600` for non-enterprise accounts.
Maya (Oncall): Confirmed: gateway rate limit applied. Monitoring telemetry now.
Elijah (SRE): Telemetry shows mean token/sec dropped ~40% post flag flip. Queue depth down 60% from peak. 429s down to baseline for most tenants but 3 high-throughput customers still seeing degraded throughput.
Lucas (Support): Who are the 3? We need to give them a direct update.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Looking at traces: those 3 have long system messages that trigger aggressive prefill behavior. Recommend targeted routing to fallback model v18-small as temporary mitigation.
Maya (Oncall): Routing rule created: route org_ids [org-783, org-119, org-402] -> model v18-small, rolling out immediately.
IncidentBot: Action log: routing-rule-create by Maya. ID ROUTE-9812.
Elijah (SRE): After routing those tenants off, their 429s cleared. Overall pool utilization falling to 72%. Autoscaler showing scale-down in progress.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Given the impact, I'm going to mark v19 rollout paused and open a revert PR. We should also add a constrained prefill-mode that respects a global token budget to prevent runaway.
Maya (Oncall): Can we confirm customer-facing impact windows so support can update SLAs?
Lucas (Support): Impact window so far: 02:09:30Z -> 02:46:10Z for broad 429 spike. For the 3 heavy tenants, marginal impact extended to 02:55Z until routing applied.
Elijah (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: v19's prefill expansion + higher default context window increased average token work per request by ~3–4x. That pushed the GPU pool to its committed cap. Autoscaler respected cap and refused scale requests, causing queue growth and frontend throttling. Secondary contributing factor: prefill warmup amplified by streaming requests, causing longer-lived KV cache state and reduced batching efficiency.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Action items I own: 1) Revert v19 -> v18 by 03:30Z if stability not confirmed; 2) Add prefill global budget flag PR; 3) Add rollout guard to block context_window increases without autoscale-profile updates.
Elijah (SRE): My actions: 1) Finish rollback playbook if needed; 2) Update autoscaler docs to call out max_pool fallback behaviors; 3) Produce telemetry slices for postmortem showing token-per-request delta.
Maya (Oncall): My actions: 1) Coordinate infra overflow if needed; 2) Keep customer comms cadence; 3) Hand off to next on-call (Maya -> Elijah 03:00Z)
Lucas (Support): I'll compile impacted org list + severity and open a support incident with names/contacts.
Elijah (SRE): Current status: stable degradation remediated by config flip + targeted routing. Pool utilization now 58%. Autoscaler no longer saturated. No further immediate action required, but we will keep the incident open for postmortem.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): I paused the rollout in the control plane to prevent re-promote.
DeployBot: Rollout v19 status: PAUSED by Zoe at 2026-03-15T02:46:35Z.
Maya (Oncall): Handing off incident to Elijah for follow-up and postmortem. Elijah, you own the follow-up. I'll remain available.
Elijah (SRE): Taking ownership for postmortem and follow-up.
Lucas (Support): One last thing: customers asked for ETA on permanent fix. Recommend we promise a full postmortem in 48 hours and a targeted rollback guard change in ~72 hours.
Zoe (Eng Runtime): Agreed.
IncidentBot: Incident state changed to 'mitigated' by Elijah at 2026-03-15T03:04:00Z.
Elijah (SRE): Closing notes: immediate mitigations: runtime prefill flag flip, targeted tenant routing to fallback model, gateway rate limits. Next steps: revert guard, budget flag, autoscale profile review, quota/overflow playbook. Postmortem ping scheduled for 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC.
Maya (Oncall): Thanks all. If anything regresses ping #incidents and escalate. :thumbsup:
